forwardMerge.how: Computed by me after a `jj git fetch`, with the procedure of skill://legion-worker/references/conflicts-and-rewrites.md, at the head my last E2E line names and at this one. The branch's own diff moved because main's 4b0b98ec2 (a Google VM signs in with its own identity token) landed two tests this branch's behaviour contradicts, and because main now imports "strings" in cmd/broker/main.go where the branch's diff used to add it.
forwardMerge.whatTheBranchChangedInIt: Two of main's own tests are adapted, nothing else of the branch's diff: internal/broker/api/vm_login_test.go's TestANarrowedVMsPendingRequestGrantsNothingWhenApproved approved a secret request through POST /v1/credential-requests/{record}/approve, which this branch refuses for every caller, so it now decides on the page through the rig's ts.decide; and cmd/broker/vm_identity_test.go's vmConfig built a configuration with no BROKER_SIGNIN_*, which this broker refuses to start without, so it carries the four from the same fixtures productionEnv uses.

implementerProof.how: I re-ran every command of the forward-merge comment at the merge head and drove the compiled binary past them. The counts reproduce: the browser suite is 53 passed and 1 skipped, the Go packages are ok, the docs site builds 43 pages, check-ci-filters passes, biome reads 793 files and tsc is clean. proof.criterion: A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A9, A10: after main's VM-identity work and the configuration it brings, the compiled broker still serves its own approval page, only the signed-in approver decides, nothing Dispatch holds decides, and a flooded bucket is refused in each class's own shape
proof.surface: my own compiled broker binary built from the merge head, on 127.0.0.1:17777 against the pod's PostgreSQL 18.6 and a real cmd/dev-oidc-issuer, two pending ALICE_DEPLOY_KEY requests seeded by real enrolled pods, driven with curl and with one pipelined socket for the floods
proof.command: curl -sL -c jar -b jar http://127.0.0.1:17777/approve/<record>; one POST /approve per refusal with the page's own hidden fields; 400 and then 500 pipelined GET /approve/<record> on one socket, with GET /signin/status, the stylesheet and POST /v1/credential-requests/<record>/approve carrying a forged bearer after them; ./broker end-sessions '  Alice@Example.COM  '
proof.observed: With no session the page is a 302 to the issuer carrying login_hint=alice@example.com, under Cache-Control: no-store, the exact Content-Security-Policy, Referrer-Policy: same-origin and X-Frame-Options: DENY. Signed in, the page prints the record's facts and both required sentences. Five refusals — no Origin, another port of the broker's own host, Origin: null, a flipped page-token character, a record the page did not print — are each 403, and the service route answers DECIDE_ON_BROKER_PAGE, with both requests still pending when I read them back. One Approve then grants one of them, with one grant, and resending that same form leaves last_decision_at at 2026-11-01T11:23:16.818788Z. The flood: 220 of 400 page loads answered 302 and 180 answered the page's own 429 under all of Cache-Control: no-store, the Content-Security-Policy, Content-Type: text/html, Referrer-Policy: same-origin, Retry-After: 1, nosniff and X-Frame-Options: DENY, naming no token; GET /signin/status on that spent bucket answered RATE_LIMITED JSON naming the address; the stylesheet answered 200. `broker end-sessions '  Alice@Example.COM  '` ended her one session and her live page then redirected to the sign-in.
proof.negativeControl: The account route's own shape needed a second, deeper flood and is the control that the three shapes are still told apart: in the first run its request landed after the bucket had refilled a token, so it reached 403 DECIDE_ON_BROKER_PAGE — the right answer for a caller with a token left — and in a 500-load run its five requests each answered 429 RATE_LIMITED naming the ServiceAccount token. So the page's refusal names no token, the public route's names the address, and the account route's names the token, as each should.

observationsForTheReviewer: The adapted TestANarrowedVMsPendingRequestGrantsNothingWhenApproved drops one assertion along with the route it replaced: the old call checked the approve route's own answer for a grant id, and the new one checks only the row's state and detail. `denied …` implies no grant, so nothing is lost in substance, but the reviewer may want that noted against main's own test.

The forward-merge comment says cmd/agent-secrets has 18 pod failures; I measure 13, the same names at this head, at the previous head and on main. The conclusion is the same and only the count is wrong.
check-ci-filters now reports 27 gates where the previous head had 28. The gate that went is main's, not this branch's; the branch's own filter entries all still match.

Standing from earlier rounds, neither a failure: a signed-in person of the domain who is not the approver is served the whole record page with no decision form, which the spec's design describes; and the page's routes share one per-address bucket with Dispatch's ServiceAccount traffic, so a deployment with a load balancer and BROKER_TRUSTED_PROXY_HEADER unset would key every browser on one address.

Still true of this pod: cmd/agent-secrets needs `-timeout 30m` (go's default ten minutes leaves the package unfinished), and a pod with no browser fails Dispatch's suite 54 of 54 in about 400 ms each until `bunx playwright install chromium`.
